title: Counting the Party a Cancellation Penalty Is Charged for on Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
When a booking sold under Air Ticket Fare Brands is given up, how many times over is the penalty owed for one traveller charged? The answer is read from two things the booking shows: the travellers it carries, and the base-fare lines standing on it.

**Where the booking carries more than one traveller and a base-fare line stands for each of them.** The penalty owed for one traveller is charged once for each traveller on the booking. A booking carrying three travellers with three base-fare lines standing on it is charged three times over.

**Where the booking carries more than one traveller and fewer base-fare lines than travellers stand on it.** The penalty owed for one traveller is charged once for each base-fare line standing on the booking. A booking carrying three travellers with two base-fare lines standing on it is charged twice over, not three times.

**In any other case.** The penalty owed for one traveller is charged once for the booking. A booking carrying a single traveller is answered here, whatever number of base-fare lines stands on it.

**Does the count follow the travellers or the lines?** It follows whichever is the smaller of the two on a booking carrying more than one traveller: the travellers where a line stands for each of them, the lines where they fall short of the travellers. Where the lines standing exceed the travellers carried, a line stands for each traveller, and the count is the travellers on the booking. In every case what is charged that many times over is the penalty owed for one traveller, settled in full.
